title: Invest in the Next Generation
speaker: Josiah Weece
summary: At church camp, a crusty old pastor said it. The church is always one generation from closing its doors. Make sure it's not yours. Following Jesus isn't a sprint or a marathon. It's a relay. And it comes down to the exchange zone.
If you're under 35, elevate your vision for your life. Josiah was 8 when he became king. So if you knew God was with you and you could not fail, what would you attempt?
If you're 35 and up, don't hang it up. In Judges 2, one generation dropped the baton. We need you. Take a young person to dinner. Pray for them. Pass the baton.

title: Help People Up
speaker: Josiah Weece
summary: Captain Sully had 208 seconds to land a plane in the Hudson. It took 42 years of small deposits to be ready. You don't get to pick the moment. You only get to pick whether you're ready. I believe our 208 seconds are coming. So we're digging ditches, and praying and fasting for 21 days.
In Acts 3, a man who couldn't walk sat by the Beautiful Gate. Everyone walked past him. But Peter stopped. He looked at him when everyone else looked away. And he helped him up.
Money can help someone out for a day. Jesus helps people up for a lifetime. This is what we do.

title: In the World, Not of It
speaker: Josiah Weece
summary: Around Austin, following Jesus doesn't make you normal. It makes you different. In John 17, Jesus prays that his followers would stay in the world without becoming like it.

It's a knife's edge, like the one on Capitol Peak. Fall off one side and you compromise, blending in until the room changes you. Fall off the other and you withdraw into a Christian bubble, away from the people God sent you to reach.
The way across is both at once. Get close to people. And stay anchored to Jesus.
